rules.sentence: One must look for mechanical ptosis in cases of infantile hemangioma, which may result in refractive and stimulus-deprivation amblyopia.[15]
Infantile hemangioma, the most common type, clinically arises in the first 8 weeks and may be present at birth.
A rapid proliferative phase ensues for 6 to 12 months, followed by an involuting, regressive phase lasting 5 to 9 years.
During the proliferative phase, the tumor presents as a raised, rubbery, and red lesion, previously termed “strawberry hemangioma.”
The involuted phase is characterized by scarring, wrinkling, and telangiectasia.[14]
